Senses.Explanation: In these records, 壓良為賤 is an accusation that someone free or worthy has been lowered and treated as base. Foyan Qingyuan applies the charge to excessive explanation; Yunmen Wenyan makes it a warning immediately before a blow, while Tianyin Yuanxiu, Feiyin Tongrong, and Huayan Shengke Deyu dispute whether a proposed distinction commits that wrong. The added records preserve the same accusation in a visiting monk’s objection to Muzhou Daoming, an unnamed monk’s reply to Dagui Zhengzhang, and statements attributed to Tiantong Jie, Jinsu Yuan, Miyun Yuanwu, and Daolin. The legal-social expression thereby serves as a public objection to how a person or claim has been ranked.

Senses.Explanation: The guest remains a guest throughout; the host remains a host throughout. Mark the Chan encounter roles before testing their exchange. Eryin Mi, Shiqi Tongyun, and Yun'e Xi use the complete saying in separate recorded teaching works. Shiyu Mingfang and Jiqi Hongchu provide further current deployments. Eryin explicitly probes beyond fixed roles, so the line is not the whole analysis.

Senses.Note: Shoushan Xingnian warns his assembly not to shout blindly. He says guest and host are each one, and that trying to make two guests and two hosts leaves both parties blind; he then tells listeners to keep their eyes sharp as they stand or sit together. A separate case source preserves this full sermon. Eryin's verse moves from frozen water to flowers opening. Xiaotang voices the line in a sermon and asks for his own guest-and-host phrase, while Linquan asks whether one can see the roles without hardening them into numbers. The phrase is a test of a shared encounter rather than a rule for formal rank.
